title: GERMAN LANGUAGE – LEVEL 04
overview: German Language – Level 04 strengthens intermediate communication skills through sustained discussion, more precise grammar, and interpretation of increasingly authentic spoken and written German. Learners practice explaining viewpoints, recounting events, comparing alternatives, handling professional interactions, and composing organized correspondence. The course emphasizes practical independence, intelligibility, cultural appropriateness, and accuracy across integrated language tasks.
audience: Learners who have completed German Language – Level 03 or have comparable pre-intermediate proficiency.
Professionals seeking greater confidence in German meetings, correspondence, and routine workplace collaboration.
Students and independent learners aiming to progress toward sustained intermediate-level communication.
methodology: Interactive lessons that connect grammar and vocabulary to communicative tasks.
Case-based dialogues, problem-solving simulations, debates, and small-group discussions.
Guided listening and reading of authentic-style interviews, reports, and professional texts.
Drafting and revision of emails, summaries, and short opinion texts with targeted feedback.
Formative skills checks, pronunciation coaching, and a final integrated assessment.
competencies: Maintain extended conversations and explain opinions with supporting arguments.
Use intermediate clause structures, past-tense forms, and case patterns with improving control.
Identify main ideas and relevant details in clear extended speech and moderately complex texts.
Prepare organized emails, descriptions, and short professional reports.
Use appropriate registers, interaction strategies, and clarification techniques in common situations.
objectives: Describe events, processes, and experiences using coherent sequencing and tense choices.
Express cause, contrast, purpose, conditions, and consequences in connected discourse.
Use relative clauses, infinitive constructions, passive forms, and Konjunktiv II in guided contexts.
Participate in practical discussions, negotiations, and workplace exchanges.
Read and summarize information from moderately challenging written and spoken sources.
Deliver a structured presentation and produce well-organized correspondence.

items.text: Review past tenses, subordinate clauses, cases, and adjective endings.
Assess listening, speaking, reading, and writing performance.
Set specific goals for fluency, grammatical control, and vocabulary growth.
Introduce and defend opinions with reasons and examples.
Signal agreement, qualified agreement, and respectful disagreement.
Use turn-taking and follow-up questions to sustain dialogue.
Contrast Perfekt and Präteritum in spoken and written contexts.
Use Plusquamperfekt to describe events preceding other past events.
Structure coherent accounts of experiences and incidents.
Use bevor, nachdem, während, seitdem, and bis appropriately.
Recognize tense relationships across main and subordinate clauses.
Describe schedules, processes, and overlapping activities.

Distinguish subordinate conjunctions from sentence adverbs.

Add identifying and supplementary information about people and objects.

Use um ... zu to express intentions and goals.

outline.title: Konjunktiv II for Politeness and Hypotheses

items.text: Use würde + infinitive and frequent forms such as hätte and wäre.
Express wishes, hypothetical possibilities, and polite requests.
Discuss alternative decisions and imagined outcomes.

outline.title: Passive Voice in Everyday and Professional Texts

items.text: Form the present and past Vorgangspassiv with werden.
Describe processes, rules, and procedures without naming the agent.
Recognize active–passive differences in notices and reports.

outline.title: Verbs with Prepositions and Pronominal Adverbs

items.text: Practice common verb–preposition combinations and required cases.

Use comparative and superlative structures in detailed evaluations.
Describe products, people, and services precisely.
Recognize frequent prefixes, suffixes, and compound nouns.
Infer meaning from word families and surrounding context.
Develop thematic vocabulary for society, work, and daily life.
Discuss education, mobility, housing, and lifestyle choices.
Compare experiences and social practices across contexts.
Support claims with examples while avoiding overgeneralization.
Give concise updates and clarify responsibilities.
Suggest actions, raise concerns, and negotiate next steps.

Write requests, confirmations, follow-ups, and explanations.
Use appropriate salutations, modal expressions, and closings.
Edit for coherence, register, and grammatical accuracy.
Explain problems, provide relevant background, and request remedies.

Use courteous negotiation language and confirmation strategies.
Explain itinerary changes, delays, and booking issues.
Compare practical alternatives and justify decisions.
Interpret announcements, terms, and service information.
